subject: BrightPoint pre-launch: temporary ingress uplift & preflight
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@brightpoint.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary ingress uplift for BrightPoint launch

Hi Lukas,

We're ramping to our public beta on Feb 2 and expect a concentrated 72-hour spike as partners hit our signup flow. Early telemetry projects ~18 requests/sec sustained with 2–3k tokens per call during peak hours (see attached forecast). Can Redwood provide a temporary ingress uplift (rate + burst headroom) for the first 7 days post-launch and a short-term SLA on throttling behavior?

Specific asks:
- Temporary rate increase to allow 25 req/s sustained with 100 concurrency headroom (region: us-west).
- Fallback routing to a lower-cost LLM variant if capacity trims are needed (we'd prefer deterministic behavior rather than opaque 429s).
- A quick runbook/point-of-contact in case we see token-level regressions.

We can commit to a short-term consumption estimate (attached) and would like an internal preflight call this week to confirm touch points.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Platform
BrightPoint Labs

Attachment: bp_launch_forecast.csv (CSV: hourly traffic projection, 7-day window)
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BrightPoint pre-launch: temporary ingress uplift & preflight

Team — forwarding BrightPoint's ask. Key asks summarized below. Can infra/product confirm feasibility and margin impact? Commercial will likely need a short-term entitlement if we commit.

Summary of external asks (BrightPoint):
- Temporary uplift to ~25 req/s sustained (us-west) for 7 days post-launch; burst concurrency ~100.
- Deterministic fallback to a lower-cost model variant rather than opaque throttling.
- Point-of-contact for on-call triage.

Questions for you:
1) Karthik — can we provision a soft cap bump for a named tenant in us-west with the requested concurrency? Would this be a Dedicated reservation carveout or a hosted temporary entitlement?
2) David — from routing/telemetry POV, can we expose deterministic fallback rules (model variant + explicit 429/502 mapping) for a tenant-level policy?
3) Marissa/Sean — commercial: what level of short-term commitment or intake do we want to tie to the uplift? Also need to confirm billing/pricing delta.

I'd like to schedule a 30-min preflight tomorrow to align owners and confirm runbook. Proposed time: Tue 27 Jan 10:00 PST. LMK if that works.

— Lukas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarded message attached: bp_launch_forecast.csv

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightPoint pre-launch: temporary ingress uplift & preflight

On Mon, Jan 26, 2026 at 08:17 AM Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding BrightPoint's ask. Key asks summarized below. Can infra/product confirm feasibility and margin impact? Commercial will likely need a short-term entitlement if we commit.

Thanks for the context. Quick technical answers:
- We can scoped-bump a hosted tenant's quota via a temporary rate profile (non-committed) for up to 30 days. That creates a soft entitlement that bypasses normal tenant-level throttles.
- For the concurrency numbers: 25 req/s at ~2.5k tokens/call is ~56k tokens/sec which is non-trivial but doable for a 1–2 node burst depending on model size. We'll need to pin a smaller variant (quantized) for the fallback path to keep latency acceptable.
- Routing: we can add a tenant-specific routing policy that switches to model_variant: redwood-small-quant when (queue_time>X ms OR token_budget_exceeded). This will surface an explicit header and status we can document.

Open items:
- Exact model baseline (which open model they want to run) — impacts memory & kernel selection.
- Whether BrightPoint wants guaranteed concurrency (reserved capacity) or a best-effort soft bump. Best-effort is faster to enable but has risk during system-wide contention.

I attached the preflight checklist we use internally. Also linking the routing playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/launch-playbook/BrightPoint-Preflight

Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime

Attachment: runtime_preflight_checklist.pdf (internal runbook)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2026 07:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightPoint pre-launch: temporary ingress uplift & preflight

Thanks — commercial view below.

- If we provide a non-committed soft bump (7 days), recommend we convert to a pre-authorized credit hold: estimate ~$4.5k for the uplift window based on their forecast (ballpark). I'll confirm with finance but we should ask BrightPoint to pre-authorize a card or sign a short amendment to the MSA.
- If they want a guaranteed reserved carve (Dedicated/reserved), that becomes a paid add-on with 1-month minimum and lead time — not realistic for their Feb 2 timeline.

Proposed commercial play:
1) Offer a 7-day soft entitlement with pre-authorized payment to cover predicted overage.
2) Require basic safety knobs: model pinning + explicit fallback to redwood-small-quant.
3) Provide an SLA for throttling behavior (we will prefer deterministic fallback; any system-wide emergency tripping will be communicated within 15 minutes).

I'll draft a short amendment and share a payment link if we agree to the soft bump. Also will own the post-launch reconciliation.

Marissa Cole
Sales Lead, GTM
Redwood Inference
